Hi, yeah, thanks. Um, well, it's... it's a lot, to be honest. What really made me come in today, like what finally pushed me to actually make the appointment, is everything going on at my job right now. I'm a buyer, I do wholesale and retail purchasing, so I'm dealing with a ton of inventory, forecasting, you know, setting up product launches and dealing with suppliers all day. It's a lot to keep track of. 

But recently, I just... I can't shake this feeling. Actually, it's more than a feeling, it's like this constant weight because I know that people at work, and even some of the external vendors we use, are tracking my buys. Like, they're secretly monitoring my purchase orders and then deliberately messing with the launch numbers behind my back just to make me look completely stupid. I know how crazy that might sound to someone on the outside, but it is happening. They're altering the data or the inventory counts to sabotage me. 

And it's just so incredibly frustrating because I tried to bring it up, I even sat down with my supervisor about it, and he pulled up all the system reports and the analytics to try and prove to me that the data doesn't show anyone tampering with anything. He spent like an hour going line by line, showing me that the reports don't prove it, but I just can't let it go because I know what I'm seeing. The numbers don't add up to what I originally put in, and it's like this whole coordinated thing between the office and the vendors to ruin my track record, and I just can't get anyone there to take it seriously... so, yeah. That's why I'm here.

Well, like I was just saying, it's not really about whether I can ignore it or not, it's more about how impossible it is to ignore someone when they sound like they're standing right on top of you. I mean, think about it. If you were just sitting there, totally alone, maybe in your car on a long stretch of highway—like when I do that drive back from the main supplier, which is a solid forty-five minutes of just me and the road—and suddenly, out of nowhere, you hear this deep, gruff man's voice right over your shoulder. My heart jumps into my throat, my hands grip the steering wheel, and I whip my head around so fast to check the backseat because my brain is telling me, 'There is a man in this car with you.' And the same thing happens at work. I'll be back in the stockroom, which is usually dead quiet because everyone else is up front, and I'm just trying to pull samples or check the physical count against the system, and suddenly he's there. Just... laughing. This mocking, condescending laugh right in my ear, like he thinks the inventory items I picked are just a joke. 

So, it's not that I feel like I *have* to do what he says, or that I can't ignore a command. It's that you physically cannot ignore the sound of another human being standing inches away from you when you know for a fact you're supposed to be alone. I turn around every single time. Every time. I look behind me in the stockroom, I check the rearview mirror, I look over my shoulder in the car, and every time... there's just nobody there. It's just empty air. But in that split second when I hear him, ignoring him isn't even an option because it's just so incredibly real and startling.

Well, you'd think so, right? Like, if things just settled down in my head, maybe that would stop too. But... no, not really. Because there was this one stretch, maybe a little while back, where things actually did get pretty quiet for me. I was finally sleeping normally again, which was huge. But the thing is, even during that calmer stretch—and this lasted for a good few weeks—I still absolutely knew they were messing with me. I still spent those entire few weeks believing people were tracking my buys. I would sit there at my desk, feeling completely physically rested, not hyped up at all, but I'd look at the purchase orders and I just knew someone was monitoring my keystrokes or altering the vendor codes to mess up my inventory counts. 

And the voice didn't stop either. I'd be back in the stockroom, totally calm, just doing a routine physical count, and I'd still hear him. That same gruff guy, right over my shoulder, even though I was sleeping great and completely level-headed about my job. So, even when everything else was fine and I wasn't feeling like some untouchable market genius, the tracking and the voice in the stockroom were still there for weeks on end. It just... it never really stops, no matter how calm I am.

It still startles me every single time I hear him, and the tracking still completely consumes my thoughts even when I'm just trying to sit on my couch and eat dinner.\n\nDoctor: Does the voice ever tell you to do something that you feel you must do, even if you don't want to?\n\nPatient: No, no, it's never like a command where I feel like I have no choice, or like I'm being controlled like a puppet or something. I whip my head around, my heart starts pounding, I drop my clipboard or I check my rearview mirror in a panic, fully expecting to see this guy standing there. I brace myself for the confrontation. But every time I turn around... there's absolutely nobody there. It's just empty space. Seeing things? Like, actually seeing a person or a shadow or something that isn't really there? No, no, I've never had anything like that happen. My eyes work just fine, I'm not seeing ghosts or anything crazy like that. 

But... you mentioned the voice, and, yeah. That's the thing that really gets to me. Because it is so incredibly real, Doc. It's not just a thought in my head or my inner monologue going rogue. It's an actual, physical sound. 

Like, I'll be down in the stockroom, right? And our stockroom is this massive, echoey concrete space down in the back of the warehouse, and usually I'm the only one down there pulling physical inventory samples to cross-reference with my purchase orders. I need to physically see the product sometimes to make sure the vendors aren't shorting us on quality. And I'll be standing there, completely alone, dead quiet except for the fluorescent lights humming, and clear as day, I hear this man's voice. It sounds like he is standing literally right behind my shoulder. And he'll just say, 'Move faster, Scott.' Just like that. Or sometimes he'll be laughing. Like this mocking, cruel laugh, specifically laughing at my picks, like he knows the vendors are messing with my numbers and he's in on the joke. 

And it's not just at the warehouse, either. Sometimes I'll be driving back from a vendor meeting—which is already incredibly stressful because I have to sit in traffic on the interstate, going over every single thing I said to make sure I didn't give them an opening to screw me over on the next shipment—and I'll hear it in my car. Same guy. Same voice. Sounding like it's coming from right behind me in the backseat. 

And every single time, whether I'm deep in the stockroom aisles or doing 70 on the highway, I whip my head around. I literally turn around because I am one hundred percent sure someone snuck up on me or somehow got into my car. But... nobody's there. It's just empty space. And I end up just standing there in the warehouse, or gripping the steering wheel so hard my knuckles turn white, trying to figure out how someone could be speaking right into my ear when I'm completely alone. So, no, I don't see anything, but hearing that guy... yeah. It happens. And it just makes everything else I have to deal with at work feel ten times heavier.
